audit.why: Packet win rate 56.62% over 136 games matches MC_WR_TABLES.zac.camille = 56.62. No elo-tier language in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: This is Zac's 11th-best matchup out of 71 at 56.62%, and it is labelled diff HARD, diffRating 8.5/10, tone #ff5d6c (the red band), with content.win giving Camille 6 of 7 stages and full.phases giving her 5 of 7. full.phases[6].side is Camille while content.win[6] is Zac, so the two layers also contradict each other on the final row, and content.late explicitly says 'the late timeline reads for you'.
audit.why: I checked the whole file rather than guessing: across all 71 Zac matchups the diff label carries no relationship to the win rate. EVEN averages 51.7%, TRICKY 53.1%, HARD 52.5%, and FAVOURED averages 48.0% — FAVOURED is applied only to 47.52% and 48.57%, which is backwards. The file's own highest win rate (Maokai, 65.75%) is labelled EVEN 6/10. So HARD 8.5/10 here is not a one-off slip; the difficulty triple is being assigned from champion archetype rather than from the data, and a player is being told they will probably lose a lane they win 56.62% of the time.
audit.corrected: For this matchup: diff EVEN, diffRating 6/10, tone #e8b84b (the file's own EVEN triple), and content.win [Camille, Camille, Camille, Skill, Camille, Zac, Zac] with full.phases matched to it. NOT proposed as edits, and deliberately so: diff HARD to EVEN and tone to tone are both length-safe, but diffRating 8.5/10 to 6/10 is -33% and breaks the band, and applying two thirds of the triple would leave the card saying EVEN next to 8.5/10. The three must move together. The file-wide pattern is the more important finding — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says to 'stay near minions so she can't ult you away' and content.spikes[1].text says 'never let her ult you away from your minions or tower'. The Hextech Ultimatum does not move the target.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area.' She travels to Zac and traps him where he already is — nothing is displaced. The advice is therefore inverted in a way that costs games: being near your own tower when the ultimate lands is good, because she has to come to you and stand in it, and the guide tells the player to treat that as the danger. Its range is also only 475, which is the shortest engage range in her kit, so it cannot be used as a long-range pick tool the way the text implies.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to state that she comes to you and anchors you in place, and gave the real 475 range and 140s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early attributes the Tactical Sweep heal to walls — 'her Q's empowered second hit and W wall-heal'. Nothing about Tactical Sweep involves walls, and the guide never states what actually triggers the heal.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Camille blasts in a cone after a delay... Enemies in the OUTER HALF are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille.' The heal and the bonus damage both come from the outer half of the cone only. That single fact is the best piece of counterplay in the matchup and it points the player the opposite way from instinct: step toward Camille to sit in the inner half and she gets neither the extra damage nor the heal. The wall requirement belongs to Hookshot, a different ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrote content.early, whys[1], wants.foe[0], dontsFull[0].d and report[8].t around the outer-half rule, and moved the wall requirement onto Hookshot where it belongs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Precision Protocol's recast is described as 'her Q's empowered second hit' and 'Q recast true damage', with no mention of the timing requirement.
audit.why: Riot's text: the recast does 'significantly increased bonus damage if Camille DELAYS a period of time between the two attacks'. The delay is the whole tell. A Camille who autos twice back to back has thrown away the spike; a Camille who pauses mid-trade is loading it. For a champion with a charged engage like Zac, reading that pause is the difference between eating the empowered hit and stepping out of it, and the guide gives the player nothing to read.
audit.corrected: Put the delay tell into content.spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot's wall requirement is never stated, even though dontsFull[2] is titled 'Fight near walls' and content.early tells the player to 'dodge her wall pins'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing.' No wall means no Hookshot — she has neither engage nor escape. The guide has a Don't card literally headed 'Fight near walls' whose body text is about blob stomping, so the one card that should carry this never says it. It also never notes that Hookshot knocks up, which matters because Zac's own engage is a knockup and whichever lands first wins the exchange.
audit.corrected: Put the wall requirement into dontsFull[2].d, dosFull[0].d, wants.you[0], whys[2], content.early and breakdown.cooldowns, and the knockup into dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json E description and terrain/hardCC flags, cd 16/15/14/13/12

audit.whatIsWrong: Adaptive Defenses is never named or described in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Basic attacks on champions grant a shield equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type (Physical or Magic).' Two things follow that matter specifically to Zac. The shield adapts to the damage type it is being hit by, so Zac's magic damage summons a magic shield rather than being a way around a physical one — there is no damage-type trick available here. And the shield is sized off HER maximum health, not Zac's, which is the opposite of Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance and is worth knowing for a champion whose whole identity is a giant health bar.
audit.corrected: Named it in whys[0] and used dontsFull[0].d, whose title is about resistance choices, to state the adapts-to-your-damage-type rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.breakdown.cooldowns gives Hookshot no number and fills its other two bullets with 'Your committal tool' and 'Your ultimate' placeholders. Its Hookshot bullet also repeats itself: 'E-knock after it. Track it before every engage.'
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s, The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s at 475 range, and Zac's Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s. Zac's own engage is on a longer cooldown than her escape at rank 1, which is exactly why the guide's repeated 'commit when Hookshot is down' instruction is harder to execute than it sounds and needs the number attached.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt the bullets around those three cooldowns and cut the repetition.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t ends 'Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind', with the wrong gender and no source named for the healing. dosFull[1] is titled 'Build armor early' and its description is the E-engage trade line instead.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this pairing and attributes it to Tactical Sweep. Since the heal only fires off the outer half of the cone, Grievous Wounds and positioning are the same answer, which is worth saying in one breath. There is also an unresolved tension the guide never acknowledges: tldr says 'Her true damage shreds your HP — build armor', and Precision Protocol does carry a true-damage component that armour cannot touch, so 'build armor' as the headline instruction against her is at best half the story.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[8].t to name Tactical Sweep as the heal and fix the pronoun, and rewrote dosFull[1].d to actually be about the armour build plus Grievous Wounds. The armour-versus-true-damage tension in tldr is flagged here rather than edited, because resolving it means deciding a build, which the kit files cannot settle.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json W and Q trueDamage flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Four Do/Don't descriptions do not match their titles. dosFull[1] 'Build armor early' carries the E-engage trade line. dosFull[2] 'E-knock her up to peel' carries a great-trade sentence. dontsFull[1] 'Get E-stunned into her combo' carries 'Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown'. dontsFull[2] 'Fight near walls' carries the blob-stomping line — the single card where the wall mechanic should have been explained.
audit.why: Same pasted-description bug as every other matchup in this slice. Here it is costliest because 'Fight near walls' is the matchup's best single piece of advice and its body text is about something else entirely.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all four to answer their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all claim stomped blobs cost 'your passive revive margin'.
audit.why: Cell Division's shed chunks are sustain and destructible; the four bloblets appear only on fatal damage and set the revive. Stomping chunks costs sustain only. Against a champion whose carry threat the file itself rates 9/10, the flat 5 minute cooldown on the revive is the number that decides whether a second all-in is survivable, and it appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Separated the two halves and stated the 5 minute cooldown.

notes: FILE-WIDE FINDING, not specific to this matchup. I checked diff / diffRating / tone against MC_WR_TABLES across all 71 Zac entries because Camille at 56.62% being labelled HARD 8.5/10 looked wrong. The labels carry essentially no signal: EVEN mean win rate 51.7% (n=33), TRICKY 53.1% (n=27), HARD 52.5% (n=8), FAVOURED 48.0% (n=2). FAVOURED is applied only to Kassadin at 47.52% and Illaoi at 48.57%, i.e. to two of the matchups Zac LOSES, which is inverted. Meanwhile the file's single best matchup, Maokai at 65.75%, is labelled EVEN. Whatever generated these assigned them from champion archetype and never looked at the data. Fixing them one matchup at a time is not worth anyone's edit budget — this wants a single pass that derives the triple from win rate, and until that happens the difficulty rating on every Zac page should be treated as decorative. Note also that the triple cannot be repaired under the current length rule even where the right answer is obvious: HARD to EVEN and the tone hex are both length-neutral, but 8.5/10 to 6/10 is -33%, so the applier would let two thirds of the change through and leave the card self-contradictory. diff, diffRating and tone need to be exempt from the band and moved atomically. Unresolved and left alone: full.tldr says 'Her true damage shreds your HP — build armor', which is in tension with itself since Precision Protocol's true-damage component ignores armour. Both halves of the advice have some merit and choosing between them is a build call, not a kit fact. Also not asserted: whether Tactical Sweep deals a percentage of maximum health. dontsFull[0] is titled 'Stack pure HP vs her W', which implies it does, but camille.json puts the percentHealth flag on the passive only, so I wrote that card from the verified outer-half rule instead of endorsing the implication.
